blocks.md: The Earth is almost a **sphere**, slightly flattened at the poles. It turns on an imaginary line called its **axis**, which joins the North Pole and the South Pole. The **Equator** is the imaginary line halfway between the poles. It divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern **Hemispheres**. The **Tropic of Cancer** (about 23½° N) and the **Tropic of Capricorn** (about 23½° S) mark the limits of the tropics.

blocks.caption: Rotation and revolution and what they cause
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows linking rotation to day and night and revolution to the year and seasons.

blocks.title: Rotation
blocks.md: **Rotation** is the spinning of the Earth on its axis. One rotation takes about **24 hours**, which is one day. The Earth turns from west to east, so the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west. At any time half of the Earth faces the Sun (day) and half faces away (night).

blocks.title: Revolution
blocks.md: **Revolution** is the movement of the Earth around the Sun. One revolution takes about **365¼ days**, which is one year. We add one extra day to February every four years to make a **leap year** of 366 days. The Earth's axis is **tilted** (about 23½°) and always points the same way in space.

Because of the tilt, the two hemispheres receive different amounts of sunlight during the year. This causes the **seasons** in places far from the Equator: when the Northern Hemisphere leans towards the Sun it has summer, while the Southern Hemisphere has winter. Near the Equator, as in most of Cameroon, the length of day changes very little, and the main seasons are the **rainy season** and the **dry season**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Rotation gives day and night; revolution gives the year. Do not swap them.
- The seasons are caused by the **tilt** of the axis, not by the Earth being closer to the Sun.
- The Sun does not move round the Earth: it only seems to, because the Earth rotates.

blocks.title: Example 1: night in Yaoundé
blocks.statement: It is noon in Yaoundé. Is it day or night on the opposite side of the Earth, and why?
steps: Half of the Earth faces the Sun at any time.
The opposite side faces away from the Sun.
So it is night there, because of rotation.
blocks.answer: It is night, because that side is turned away from the Sun.

blocks.title: Example 2: leap years
blocks.statement: How many days are there in four ordinary years plus one extra leap day, if each ordinary year has 365 days?
steps: This is why the real year is about 365¼ days.
